2609.22281.title: Performance vs Consistency: Evaluating a Foundation Model in Lung-RADS Screening
2609.22281.paper_summary: Foundation models have recently demonstrated strong capabilities across a wide range of medical imaging tasks. However, their performance in structured clinical interpretation settings remains insufficiently explored. In lung cancer screening, interpretative variability persists despite standardized frameworks such as Lung-RADS. In this study, we evaluate MedGemma, a medical general-purpose foundation model derived from Gemini and its fine-tuned version adapted for lung cancer detection and diagnosis, compared against radiologists performing Lung-RADS v2022 assessment on the NLST dataset. Twelve radiologists independently evaluated each case in a multi-reader design, enabling quantification of inter-reader variability. Radiologists achieved a mean AUC of 0.90, with substantial variability across readers (range: 0.80-0.94). The native foundation model achieved an AUC of 0.70, failing to reach clinically relevant performance. In contrast, fine-tuning significantly improved performance to an AUC of 0.83, placing the model within the lower range of individual radiologists performance. These findings highlight a trade-off between peak accuracy and prediction consistency. Unlike radiologists, under fixed conditions, the model produces deterministic outputs, removing inter-run variability under identical inputs, in contrast to inter-reader variability observed among radiologists. This supports the role of fine-tuned foundation models potential complementary tools for clinical decision support, particularly in settings with limited expertise. However, evaluation is performed on a case-enriched cohort from NLST and does not account for real-world prevalence or external validation, limiting direct clinical generalization.
2609.22281.paper_summary_zh: 基礎模型最近在廣泛的醫學影像任務中展示了強大的能力。<lb/>然而，它們在結構化臨床解釋環境中的表現仍然不足以深入探討。<lb/>在肺癌篩檢中，儘管有像 Lung-RADS 這樣的標準化框架，解釋變異性依然存在。<lb/>在這項研究中，我們評估了 MedGemma，這是一個源自 Gemini 的醫療通用基礎模型及其針對肺癌檢測和診斷的微調版本，並與在 NLST 數據集上執行 Lung-RADS v2022 評估的放射科醫生進行比較。<lb/>十二位放射科醫生在多讀者設計中獨立評估每個案例，使得讀者之間的變異性得以量化。<lb/>放射科醫生的平均 AUC 為 0.90，但讀者之間的變異性相當大（範圍：0.80-0.94）。<lb/>原始基礎模型的 AUC 為 0.70，未能達到臨床相關的表現。<lb/>相比之下，微調顯著提高了性能，達到 AUC 0.83，使該模型位於個別放射科醫生表現的下限範圍內。<lb/>這些發現突顯了峰值準確性與預測一致性之間的權衡。<lb/>與放射科醫生不同，在固定條件下，該模型產生確定性的輸出，消除了在相同輸入下的運行間變異性，這與放射科醫生之間觀察到的讀者變異性形成對比。<lb/>這支持了微調基礎模型作為臨床決策支持潛在補充工具的角色，特別是在專業知識有限的環境中。<lb/>然而，評估是在 NLST 的案例豐富隊列上進行的，並未考慮現實世界的流行率或外部驗證，限制了直接的臨床推廣。
